verdict.rationale: Mastra's pricing page offers free self-hosting of Mastra projects under an Apache 2.0 license, "Build and host agents anywhere". Its deployment docs say apps run on any Node.js-compatible environment (also Bun, Deno, Cloudflare), as a standalone Mastra server or inside an existing web framework. Studio also runs locally at localhost:4111. A community comment calls an earlier license Elastic v2, but that still permits self-hosting, so it does not contradict this capability. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted production deployment, and consistent licensing evidence (Apache 2.0 vs the earlier Elastic v2 report).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Self host your Mastra projects ... Free Apache 2.0 licensed $0/ month ... Build and host agents anywhere
Mastra applications can be deployed to any Node.js-compatible environment. You can deploy a Mastra server or integrate with an existing web framework.
Mastra can run against any of these runtime environments: - Node.js `v22.13.0` or later - Bun - Deno - Cloudflare
Open Studio at [`http://localhost:4111`](http://localhost:4111) to test your agent and inspect its runs.
